title: STR-Bamba: Multimodal Molecular Textual Representation Encoder-Decoder Foundation Model
experiments_summary: The study employed the following methods and experiments: (1) Custom BPE tokenizer construction trained on ~28 million samples across seven molecular modalities (SMILES, SELFIES, IUPAC name, InChI, molecular formula, SPG polymer notation, electrolyte formulations), with modality-specific pre-tokenization steps and a unified vocabulary of 5000 tokens. (2) Pre-training of the STR-Bamba 426M encoder-decoder hybrid Transformer/Mamba-2 model on ~588 million samples (~29 billion tokens) derived from 117 million PubChem small molecules, ~2 million synthetic/real polymers, and 258 electrolyte formulations, using two-stage training: Phase 1 trained only the encoder using masked language modeling and sentence-level alignment (same/different molecule classification) on 396 NVIDIA A100 GPUs; Phase 2 trained only the decoder for next-token generation conditioned on encoder embeddings on 8 NVIDIA A100 GPUs. (3) Latent space analysis using t-SNE projections of encoder embeddings from 2000 random samples per modality (all 258 formulation samples), followed by K-means clustering with cluster counts varied from 2 to 10, evaluated with Davies-Bouldin Index, Adjusted Rand Index, V-Measure, and Fowlkes-Mallows Score. (4) Property prediction benchmarking across 29 datasets (99 tasks total) covering MoleculeNet classification and regression tasks for small molecules, 26 polymer property prediction tasks from multiple literature datasets, and 2 electrolyte formulation prediction tasks; individual modalities and all possible modality combinations (325 combinations) were evaluated with TPE optimization on validation sets to identify top-3 combinations per task; all experiments used five random seeds with fixed train/validation/test splits. (5) Molecular representation translation evaluation on 3007 random training molecules, assessing SMILES-to-SELFIES and SELFIES-to-SMILES translation using RDKit validity checks and Tanimoto similarity, and IUPAC name and molecular formula generation using BLEU-1, BLEU-2, and Jaccard similarity metrics.
